groups.label: Names for the practice
groups.about: Labels for the work of setting an agent up well. They overlap, and new ones keep appearing.

groups.label: What the model sees
groups.about: Everything that reaches the model goes through its context window.

groups.label: How the agent acts
groups.about: The loop that runs the model's tool calls, and the limits on what they can touch.

groups.label: What checks the work
groups.about: The checks that catch mistakes while the agent is still working.

terms.definition: Writing the request so the model understands it.
Choosing everything that goes into the context window, not only the prompt.
A recent name for designing the instructions, checks and limits around an agent.
The built-in instructions that tell the model how to behave and how to use its tools.
Everything the model sees on a turn, and the only thing it sees.
A file of project instructions the agent reads at the start: how to build, how to test, what to avoid.
Packaged instructions that load in full only when a task needs them.
Notes the agent keeps on disk and loads in later sessions.
Summarizing older turns when the context fills up. It frees space, and can lose detail.
The runtime that calls the model, runs its tool calls, and feeds the results back until the task is done.
The Model Context Protocol: an open standard for connecting agents to external tools and data.
Separate agents with their own context, which return a short summary.
A separate checkout per task, so agents work in isolation and in parallel.
Rules on what the agent may run without asking, and limits on what any command can touch.
Guides steer the agent before it acts; sensors check its work after. Each is either a deterministic tool or a model.
Scripts the agent loop runs on events. They can block a tool call, or feed a check's output back to the model.
A model that checks output against a rubric, for quality that rules cannot measure.
Scheduled agent runs that look for drift and open small fix pull requests.
